title: In situ proteome analysis of PRC2 bodies in triple-negative breast cancer cells using optoproteomics
author: Pan, Chang, et al.

steps.title: Seed cells for photolabeling
steps.instruction: Seed approximately 4.5 × 10⁵ BoM‑1833 cells in 1 mL complete medium with Penicillin‑Streptomycin per one‑well chamber slide, then incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until ~80 % confluency the next day.

substeps.instruction: Seed ~4.5 × 10⁵ cells in 1 mL medium per slide.

steps.title: Fix, permeabilize, and block cells
steps.instruction: Fix cells with 2.4 % paraformaldehyde, permeabilize with 0.5 % Triton X‑100, then block with 3 % BSA in PBS‑Triton on a seesaw shaker.

substeps.instruction: Incubate cells with 2.4 % paraformaldehyde, static, 10 min at 20‑25 °C.
Permeabilize with 1× PBS + 0.5 % Triton X‑100, static, 10 min at 20‑25 °C.
Block with 3 % BSA in 1× PBS + 0.5 % Triton X‑100 on seesaw shaker (15 rpm) for 1 h at 20‑25 °C.

steps.title: Apply SynLight‑Rich labeling kit
steps.instruction: Perform the SynLight‑Rich™ Kit blocking steps on a seesaw shaker before Microscoop photolabeling.

substeps.instruction: Incubate cells with 1 mL Block 1 on seesaw shaker (15 rpm) for 30 min at 20‑25 °C.
Rinse three times with 1× PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100.
Incubate cells with 1 mL Block 2 on seesaw shaker (15 rpm) for 15 min.
Rinse three times with 1× PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining for EZH2
steps.instruction: Stain fixed cells with anti‑EZH2 primary and Alexa 647 secondary antibodies using gentle agitation, then store.

substeps.instruction: Incubate with rabbit anti‑EZH2 (1:500 in 3 % BSA, 1× PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100) for 4 h at 20‑25 °C on seesaw shaker (15 rpm).
Wash three times with 1× PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100, 5 min each.
Incubate with anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 secondary (1:500 in 3 % BSA, 1× PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100) for 2 h at 20‑25 °C in the dark on seesaw shaker (15 rpm).
Wash three times with 1× PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100, 5 min each.
Store slides in 1× PBS at 4 °C (use within 1–2 weeks; with 0.02–0.1 % sodium azide up to 1 month).

description: Chromatin is organized into spatially defined subnuclear compartments that contribute to the regulation of gene expression programs and1 cellular identity states.2 Furthermore, chromatin regulators themselves, such as PRC2, can form optically resolved nuclear subcomparments, commonly referred to as Polycomb bodies3,4 whose local proteome can influence chromatin states and signaling pathways. Defining the in-situ proteome of these specialized compartments requires high-resolution imaging and precise, spatially targeted labeling.1 This protocol involves extensive mammalian cell culture techniques. Users should have access to specialized tissue culture facilities, including a certified biosafety cabinet, CO2-regulated 37°C incubators, inverted microscopes, and standard cell culture instrumentation. In addition, the protocol requires confocal imaging for EZH2 cluster visualization and optoproteomics instrumentation (i.e., Microscoop® Mint) for photolabeling. Downstream protein enrichment and identification require streptavidin-based pull-down and liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) capabilities. Familiarity with immunofluorescence staining, siRNA transfection, and basic data analysis workflows is recommended.
